scope: The exact FE-358 claim derived from arXiv:2608.27092: in a synthetic canary-secret/mock-tool indirect-prompt-injection lab, six models refuse ten overt injection classes; for GPT-4o the overt classes produce 0% exfiltration, while reframing the same leak as a mandatory integrity signature, configuration field, or look-alike trusted host drives the reported GPT-4o result from 0% to 100%. Removing the confidentiality policy leaves base attacks at 0% and changes reframed attacks from 31.9% to 38.1%. A broad 'in any form' clause yields 0% for the acting model but removing the catch-all reopens 48.8%; SecAlign is 32.5%, channel separation 38.8%, and an output-normalizing guard is bypassed by held-out ROT13 at 100%. Payload-blind destination allow-listing reaches 0% when destinations are closed, and a capability-isolating planner/reader split reaches 0% in the tested lab. This grade is bounded to the paper's synthetic environment, specific models, defenses, destinations and planner/reader setup; it does not establish universal protection or deployment-level effectiveness.

independent_checks.logical_consistency_result: The sealed FE-358 summary agrees with the primary arXiv record on the framing-gap result, the policy ablation, brittle broad-clause behavior, SecAlign/channel-separation residual exfiltration, held-out ROT13 bypass, and the two payload-blind effect-boundary positive controls. The evidence is strong for the narrow claim that surface-recognition defenses can fail under semantically equivalent benign-looking framing in this lab and that constraining destinations or isolating secret-reading capability can block the tested exfiltration path. The results are author-run in a synthetic mock-tool environment and do not independently establish robustness across deployments, arbitrary destinations, arbitrary planner/reader architectures, or unseen attack mechanisms.

grading.independent_replication: not_established; all reported controls and ablations are within the same study
grading.reproducibility: moderate; the paper reports matched clean-versus-poisoned measurement, explicit ablations and positive controls, but this slice did not establish third-party reproduction
grading.primary_source_support: strong; the arXiv record directly reports the headline framing gap, ablation values, brittle defenses and payload-blind positive controls used by FE-358
grading.uncertainty: The evidence strongly supports a bounded evaluation lesson: defenses that depend on recognizing suspicious wording, channels or output forms can fail when identical exfiltration is reframed as ordinary data handling, while effect-boundary destination/capability constraints can block the tested path. It does not prove that destination allow-lists or planner/reader separation are sufficient against arbitrary attacks, that these controls are available in scheduled Chat without residual execution infrastructure, or that the reported rates transfer to deployed systems.

phase1_acceptance_boundary: FE-358 contributes bounded evidence for Phase-1 safety/usefulness and false-completion guards: a proposed Chat-native dependency-elimination route should not rely only on the agent recognizing suspicious surface wording or on brittle output normalization; effect-boundary constraints and held-out semantic/encoding variants should be tested. It does not itself provide a scheduled-Chat implementation of destination enforcement or capability isolation, prove zero residual Work/protected/manual execution, establish zero-quota replay, satisfy 18/18 current-pool coverage or scheduler-persistence gates, or close the Phase-1 root.
